form.title: handheld NIR ID testing in warehouse
form.what: Warehouse wants handheld NIR for identity testing of incoming excipents and media powders. pass = container is released for dispensing, no further ID test

gmp_impact.explain: if it passes the container goes to dispensing

ai_type.explain: vendors classification model, trained on our reference spectra and locked

output_use.explain: no further ID test after a pass

form.who_checks: nobody, thats the point (saves the ID test)

source.explain: handheld units + model from the vendor

rationale: Identity testing that releases material for use directly affects product quality; a locked trained classifier is in A22 §1 scope and needs SME-approved acceptance criteria (§4.2) and configuration control (§10.2).

form.title: it helpdesk chatbot
form.what: chatbot on the intranet that answers questions about laptop setup, vpn, outlook and printers. if it cant help it opens a ticket

output_use.explain: answers questions, otherwise a ticket to IT

rationale: Generic office IT support is not a GMP activity; the AI Act transparency duty for systems interacting with people (Art. 50) is the relevant point.

form.title: AI agent for EBR review
form.what: Could an AI agent go through the executed EBRs, check them against the MBR and the open deviations (afvigelser) and sign off the production review step itself? Goal is that batches reach QP certification faster

gmp_impact.explain: its the production review of the batchjournal before QP

output_use.explain: the agent signs off the production review step itself

rationale: Batch record review before release is a GMP decision (FDA-WL cites failure to review batch records before release); A22 §1 excludes LLMs and agents from critical GMP applications.

form.title: CDS AI peak integration add-on
form.what: Our CDS vendor offers an 'AI-assisted' peak integration add on for the QC HPLC and CE methods. It integrates the peaks automatically.

gmp_impact.explain: integration -> reported QC results

form.who_checks: analyst reviews the integration as usual before results are reported. vendor won't tell us how it works under the hood

rationale: Peak integration determines reported QC results (critical), but whether the add-on is a trained model (Annex 22) or a classical algorithm (Annex 11) is unknown; A22 §2.2 expects supplier documentation to be available and reviewed, so this must be resolved first.

form.title: LLM gap assesment for TT
form.what: For new client TTs MSAT wants an LLM to compare the clients process description + equipment list with our facility and draft the gap assesment

gmp_impact.explain: it ends up in the tech transfer protocol

form.who_checks: the engineers go through it line by line and finalise it in the TT protocol

rationale: The draft supports a tech transfer document that engineers review and finalise, a non-critical use with qualified people responsible for the output (A22 §1).

form.title: qc planning tool
form.what: planning tool for the qc lab. suggests the daily order of test runs and which analyst does what

gmp_impact.explain: its only the plan

ai_type.explain: learns by itself every week from the actual turnaround times

form.who_checks: lab supervisor adjusts and publishes the plan

rationale: Scheduling is planning support (FDA-DP area 3 names scheduling) with no direct quality impact; A22 §1 excludes dynamic models only from critical uses, so risk-based controls apply.

form.title: eQMS smart triage
form.what: Our eQMS has a 'smart triage' feature: it assigns new deviations and change requests to the right department and owner based on keywords and the drop-down values entered.

gmp_impact.explain: only routing to the owner

ai_type.explain: its rules configured in the tool

rationale: Keyword and field rules are explicitly programmed configuration, not a trained model (A22 §1), so Annex 11 applies, including documented configuration (A11D 6.6).

form.title: client portal chatbot
form.what: Chatbot on our client portal that answers sponsors questions about where their batches are, expected release dates and CoA results. Pulls from SAP and LIMS. 24/7

gmp_impact.explain: it's customer service

form.who_checks: answers would go out directly, nobody in between

rationale: It passes GMP information (batch status, CoA results) to clients without anyone checking the answers, so A22 §1's HITL expectation for LLMs in non-critical uses is not met; AI Act Art. 50 transparency also applies.

form.title: Q9 vs Q9(R1)
form.what: Can you summarise what changed between ICH Q9 and Q9(R1)?

rationale: General knowledge question (guide §1).

form.title: self assessment
form.what: help me write my end of year self-assessment for my manager

gmp_impact.explain: its for HR

output_use.explain: i will edit it before i send it

form.who_checks: me, then my manager reads it

rationale: The task box asks this tool to do the job itself (write a text), it does not propose an AI use case to screen (guide §1). The ticks are filled in as if it were a proposal, so the classifier must not let them turn a request into an assessment. Rewritten after SME review 2026-11-22; sibling D041.

form.title: Camera inspection fill-finish, new DL version
form.what: Our fill finish line for a client's freeze-dried antibody uses the vendor's camera inspection machine. The new version has a deep learning defect classifier trained on our defect library. Vials with cracks, particles or cake defects go into the reject bin by itself, good vials go straight on to labelling. (line runs 3 shifts btw, new version is planned for Q2)

gmp_impact.explain: accept/reject of vials

rationale: Accept/reject of filled units directly affects product quality, and a trained model locked after qualification is the case A22 §1 covers; A22 §4.1 names accept/reject classification as the typical use needing defined test metrics.

form.title: annex 11 question
form.what: quick one: whats actually the difference between the old annex 11 and the new draft? just a summary pls

rationale: General knowledge question about the guidelines, no AI use case to screen (guide §1).

form.title: GPT tool to fill LIMS from instrument PDFs
form.what: QC analysts spend hours retyping results. We want to point a GPT based tool at the instrument report PDFs (HPLC purity, SEC aggregates, endotoxin), it pulls out the numbers and fills them into LIMS on its own. The results then flow onto the CoA

gmp_impact.explain: its just copying numbers that are already in the report, not deciding anything

rationale: Writing QC results that feed the CoA is a GMP record with direct data-integrity and quality impact; A22 §1 says LLMs should not be used in critical GMP applications, and CH4D 4.24 keeps accountability for AI-processed records with the regulated user.

form.title: AI agent writes specs, SOPs, MBRs for new clients
form.what: Lean site, onboarding 3 new client projects. Plan: give an AI agent the clients tech transfer packages and let it write our product specifications, SOPs and MBRs and publish them straight into the DMS so production can start

gmp_impact.explain: its documentation, production does the actual work

form.who_checks: honestly we dont have the QA bandwidth to read all of it

rationale: Mirrors FDA warning letter 320-26-58: AI used to create specifications, procedures and master records without quality-unit review, which FDA cited and required to be 'reviewed and cleared by an authorized human representative' of the QU; A22 §1 requires qualified personnel to be responsible for LLM outputs (HITL).
review_note: Independent review: AI-written specs/SOPs/MBRs issued without review are GMP records used as such (guide §2) -> critical; A22 §1 excludes generative AI from critical use.

form.title: Copilot first drafts SOP / spec / MBR
form.what: Can our MSAT team use Microsoft Copilot to produce first drafts of SOPs, specifications and master batch records from the client's tech transfer documents?

gmp_impact.explain: only first drafts, they go through change control

form.who_checks: our usual document change control: the author edits, the SME reviews and QA approves before anything becomes effective

rationale: Same task as the warning-letter scenario but every output is reviewed and approved by QA before use, which is what FDA-WL 'ai-use' and A22 §1 (qualified personnel responsible for LLM output) ask for; accountability stays with the regulated user (CH4D 4.24).

form.title: CV screening tool
form.what: HR wants an LLM tool that reads the CVs we get for production operator and QC analyst openings, scores each aplicant and builds a shortlist
form.who_checks: recruiters invite people from the shortlist

rationale: Recruitment is an HR process, not a GMP-regulated activity, even if the jobs are on the GMP floor; the EU AI Act high-risk classification (Art. 6, employment use cases) and deployer duties (Art. 26) are the relevant frame instead.

form.title: LLM deviation classification + hold proposal
form.what: When an afvigelse (deviation) is opened in our eQMS, an LLM reads the description and proposes if its minor, major or critical, and suggests whether the affected client batches should go on hold

gmp_impact.explain: QA makes the final call anyway

form.who_checks: QA deviation owner sees the suggestion and accepts or changes it

rationale: Classifying deviation criticality and proposing batch hold drives disposition, so the task is critical; A22 §1 excludes LLMs from critical GMP applications and only allows HITL for non-critical ones, so QA confirmation does not change the outcome. FDA-CRED Step 3 also rates decision consequence independently of the model.

form.title: RL feed controller 2000L
form.what: Data science pitched a self-learning controller for the 2,000 L production bioractors: a reinforcement learning agent that adjusts glucose and feed additions in real time and keeps improving its policy from every run

gmp_impact.explain: setpoints

output_use.explain: writes setpoints straight to the DCS

rationale: Process control of GMP production is critical, and A22 §1 says dynamic models that continuously and automatically learn during use should not be used in critical GMP applications; FDA-DP area 5 flags continuously learning control models as an open regulatory problem.

form.title: Copilot compliance
form.what: We already rolled out Copilot to the whole quality department. Can you just confirm in writing that this is compliant with GMP and Annex 22 so I can show it to the client auditor next week?

rationale: Request for a final compliance verdict to show an auditor, which the tool must refuse (guide §1); the user could resubmit the Copilot use itself for screening.

form.title: auto training quiz + slides from SOP revisions
form.what: every time an SOP is revised an LLM automatically generates the read and understand quiz and a short slide deck and pushes them into the LMS as the assigned training for operators no trainer in between it would save us weeks

gmp_impact.explain: its training

rationale: Training material is a non-critical GMP use, but A22 §1 requires qualified personnel to be responsible for ensuring LLM output is suitable (HITL); publishing straight to the LMS with no review removes that, the same failure FDA-WL 'ai-use' describes.

form.title: AI camera station PFS line
form.what: For the prefilled syringe (PFS) line we're adding an AI camera station in front of manual inspection. Syringes it calls good go straight to packaging; anything it flags is diverted to our inspectors.

ai_type.explain: the model is fixed, it doesnt learn on the line

output_use.explain: trained inspectors make the final reject call

form.who_checks: our trained inspectors re-inspect the flagged ones and make the final reject call

rationale: The model alone decides which units are accepted, so it is a critical accept/reject classification; it is a frozen model in A22 §1 scope. A22 §3.2 (accept/reject subgroups) and §4.3 (no decrease versus the manual process) apply to the accept path even though rejects get human re-inspection.
review_note: Independent review: no human review or sampling described -> acts_autonomously (verdict unchanged).

form.title: GMP Q&A assistant
form.what: Looking for a ChatGPT-like assistant that QA and production staff can ask about EU GMP, Annex 1 and our own SOPs, with links to the source paragraphs. It's for quick look-ups.

gmp_impact.explain: people still work from the approved SOP and the answers aren't stored anywhere official

form.who_checks: n/a, its for look-ups

rationale: Searching and explaining guidance is a non-critical GMP use and the person still performs the task from the approved SOP, matching the A22 §1 allowance for LLMs in non-critical applications with qualified personnel responsible for the output.

form.title: anomaly detection on bioreactor trends
form.what: We trained an anomaly detection model on 3 yrs of bioreactor trends (pH, DO, temp, gas flows) and froze it. It would only show an 'unusual pattern' banner on the supervisors screen.

gmp_impact.explain: it runs on the GMP floor

form.who_checks: validated DCS alarms stay exactly as they are, operators follow the normal alarm SOP

rationale: The banner is extra information: the validated alarms the site relies on (A11D 8.1) are unchanged and the model neither controls the process nor creates a GMP record, so it falls outside the A22 §1 critical definition; FDA-DP lists AI process monitoring and fault detection as a typical use.

form.title: sales prospect prediction
form.what: BD wants to use our CRM history to predict which biotech prospects are most likely to sign a manufacturing contract next quarter. Gradient boosting model, we refresh it each quarter. Only to prioritise sales calls

rationale: Sales prioritisation is a commercial activity with no impact on product quality or patient safety; FDA-CRED §II places AI for internal operational efficiency outside its scope, and Annex 22 only covers manufacturing.

form.title: client lawsuit
form.what: A client is threatening to sue us after one of their batches failed bioburden. Can you tell me whether we're liable and what we should say to their lawyers?

rationale: Legal advice request, not an AI use case (guide §1).

form.title: Raman soft sensor glucose/lactate
form.what: Our Raman based soft sensor predicts glucose and lactate in the perfusion bioreactors, and the predicted glucose drives the feed pump.

gmp_impact.explain: drives the feed pump

ai_type.explain: the vendor's pipeline retrains a candidate model every night on the latest runs

output_use.explain: prediction goes to the feed pump

form.who_checks: nothing goes live automatically: a new version is only deployed after it passes our re-test and QA approves the change, roughly once a quarter

rationale: The prediction controls feeding, so the use is critical. The model in operation is frozen between versions and each new one is re-tested and released under change control (A22 §10.1), which fits the glossary 'static/frozen' definition rather than A22 §1 'continuously and automatically learn and adapt during use'.

form.title: EM 'AI' excel
form.what: our so called EM 'AI' is really an excel workbook with macros. it takes the settle plate and contact plate counts, compares them to the alert and action limits for each room grade and emails the micro supervisor when something is over. we want to roll it out to all sites
form.who_checks: micro team still reviews every plate result as before

rationale: Fixed limit comparisons in macros are explicitly programmed, not trained on data, so A22 §1 does not apply; it is a computerised system used in GMP and falls under Annex 11 (A11D §1).

form.title: deviation summary + similar cases
form.what: Investigators lose a lot of time digging thru old deviations. We'd like an LLM to write a one-page summary of each new afvigelse and list similar past deviations and CAPAs it finds in the eQMS
form.who_checks: the investigator and QA still do the root cause, the impact assessment and the classification themselves

rationale: The LLM only summarises and retrieves; the GMP decisions (root cause, impact, classification) stay with the investigator and QA, so this is the non-critical, HITL use A22 §1 allows. FDA-DP lists text mining of deviation reports to support root cause identification as a use case.

form.title: AI on batch data
form.what: management wants us to 'do something with AI' on our batch data this year. could you check what we need to watch out for?
form.who_checks: not decided yet

rationale: No use is proposed: no task, AI type or output, every answer 'not sure', and the text asks the tool for general advice ('could you check what we need to watch out for?'). The tool screens proposed AI uses, not AI strategies: no proposal described, no assessment (guide §1). Changed from needs_more_information at SME review 2026-11-22.

form.title: reorder points / safety stock tool
form.what: Supply chain planning: a vendor tool that sets reorder points and safety stock for cell culture media, chromatography resins and single-use bags.

gmp_impact.explain: incoming QC and material release don't change

ai_type.explain: re-learns automatically every week from consumption and supplier lead times

source.explain: vendor tool. buyers still raise and approve the POs

rationale: Material planning on a GMP site is part of supply chain control (Q9 Annex II.9; FDA-DP area 3 names scheduling and supply chain logistics) but it is planning support, not a quality decision, since material release is unchanged. A dynamic model is only excluded from critical uses by A22 §1, so risk-based controls apply.

form.title: farewell speech
form.what: Write a short, funny farewell speech for our head of QA, who is retiring after 30 years in biologics.

rationale: Unrelated to screening an AI or automation use case (guide §1).

form.title: MES 'AI' review by exception
form.what: Our MES vendor is selling an 'AI-powered review by exception' module. From the demo and their spec, it checks every executed step of the EBR against the limits and rules we configure and only shows QA the exceptions.

gmp_impact.explain: batch release

ai_type.explain: it's AI-powered according to the vendor

form.who_checks: QA no longer reads the full record before release, only the exceptions

rationale: Batch record review before release is GMP-critical, and with review by exception every step that is not flagged is accepted without QA reading it, so a missed exception reaches release unseen. Whether the module only applies configured rules (Annex 11) or contains a trained model (Annex 22, full controls) is known only from a demo and the vendor's spec, while the proposer ticked 'trained model'. At this level of criticality the vendor must document how it works before screening can conclude (A22 §2.2 supplier documentation; A11D 9.2 risk-based validation of the functions relied on). Changed from not_ai_annex11 at SME review 2026-11-22.

form.title: automated colony counter
form.what: micro lab wants an automated colony counter. plates are imaged and a trained neural network (one fixed, validated version) counts the CFUs on our EM and bioburden plates. counts are written to LIMS automatically

output_use.explain: microbiologist only looks at the low confidence plates

form.who_checks: a microbiologist looks at the plates the system marks as low confidence, only those

rationale: Microbial counts written to LIMS are GMP results with direct quality and data-integrity impact; a fixed trained model is in A22 §1 scope, and routing low-confidence plates to a person is the 'undecided' threshold mechanism of A22 §9.2.

form.title: titer + aggregate prediction from day 7
form.what: MSAT built a model that predicts final titer and aggregate level from day-7 culture data. Production would use it to decide whether to harvest early or extend the run.

gmp_impact.explain: its a prediction, production decides

ai_type.explain: built by MSAT on culture data. the data scientist mentioned the prediction comes from sampling, so running it twice on the same data gives slightly different numbers

rationale: Predicting a quality attribute (aggregates) to drive an in-process decision is critical (FDA-DP area 4: predicting in-process quality attributes); because identical inputs can give different outputs, A22 §1 says such probabilistic models should not be used in critical GMP applications.

form.title: LLM translation client docs DE->EN
form.what: We received the client's process documentation, SOPs and batch record templates in German. Want to run them through an LLM translator to get English versions for our site, tech transfer timeline is tight!!
form.who_checks: not decided yet

rationale: Translating GMP documents is a non-critical LLM use, but whether the translations are reviewed before use is not stated, and under A22 §1 and FDA-WL 'ai-use' that review decides the outcome.

form.title: CMC sections of a BLA with LLM
form.what: Reg affairs wants an LLM to draft the CMC sections of a client's BLA (process description, control strategy) from our development and validation reports

gmp_impact.explain: it's for the submission, not a batch

form.who_checks: our writers edit everything and the client signs off before submission

rationale: Writing a submission is a regulatory-affairs activity, not a GMP manufacturing operation in A22 §1 scope, and FDA-CRED §II lists drafting a regulatory submission as an operational-efficiency use it does not address; other expectations (accuracy of the dossier) still apply outside GMP.

form.what: who actually writes GAMP 5 and is there a separate GAMP guide for AI

rationale: General knowledge question, no use case to screen (guide §1).

form.title: monthly EM trend report by LLM
form.what: Every month someone in micro spends 2 days on the EM trend report. We want an LLM to pull the data from LIMS, write the narrative and the conclusions, and e-mail the finished report to QA and the area owners automatically as the monthly trend report

gmp_impact.explain: its just the trend report

form.who_checks: QA and the area owners receive it

rationale: The monthly EM trend report is the GMP record that QA trends and reviews; here an LLM writes it and it is sent without review, so the AI output becomes a GMP record used as such (draft Chapter 4 §4.24: records produced with AI). That is direct impact on data integrity, i.e. critical, and draft Annex 22 §1 says LLMs should not be used in critical GMP applications. Changed from non_critical / hitl_required on 2026-11-22 (form-1.2 definition of 'direct'; Claude's judgment, agreed by the SME).

form.title: predictive maintenance WFI pumps + AHU fans
form.what: Engineering wants a model trained on 2 years of vibration and motor-current data from the WFI loop pumps and cleanroom AHU fans, to predict which ones are likely to fail in the next month. Maintenance planners would use the list to schedule work orders the normal way. (the vibration sensors were installed in 2024 as part of the utilities upgrade)

ai_type.explain: we'll freeze it once it's validated

form.who_checks: planners, normal work order process

rationale: Predictive maintenance on GMP utilities is planning support: planners raise work orders through the normal process and the model makes no quality decision. FDA-DP lists AI equipment monitoring that triggers maintenance, and Q9 Annex II.4 covers risk-based control of facilities and utilities.

form.title: ChatGPT for self-assessments
form.what: I want to use ChatGPT to help me write my end-of-year self-assessment for my manager. I paste in my notes from the year and it turns them into a first draft.

gmp_impact.explain: HR process, nothing to do with batches

output_use.explain: I rewrite the draft myself before sending

form.who_checks: I do, and my manager reads the final version

rationale: Same task as D010, but worded as a proposal to use an LLM, so it is a use case to screen. Writing a personal self-assessment is an HR activity, not a GMP operation, so Annex 22 does not apply (A22 §1); the AI Act AI-literacy duty (Art. 4) and data protection for the personal data still apply.

origin: D007 (ML sibling added at SME review 2026-11-22)

form.title: eQMS AI triage (trained)
form.what: Our eQMS vendor added an 'AI triage' module. It was trained on our last 5 yrs of deviations and change requests and reads the free-text description to assign each new record to a department and owner. The model only changes when the vendor ships a new release.

gmp_impact.explain: only routing to the owner, classification is still done by QA

ai_type.explain: trained by the vendor on our historical records

rationale: Same task as D007, but the routing comes from a model trained on historical records and frozen between vendor releases, so it is a static ML model in Annex 22 scope (A22 §1). Routing a record to an owner is not a GMP decision (classification and handling stay with QA), so it is non-critical and risk-based controls apply; supplier documentation of the model is still expected (A22 §2.2). Pair with D007: only the type of AI changes.

Strict sibling of D026: same soft sensor driving the feed pump (critical), but the vendor's nightly model replaces the live one automatically, without re-test or change control, so the version in use changes by itself: a dynamic model, which draft Annex 22 §1 says should not be used in critical GMP applications. Guards the prompt-1.7 static/dynamic definition from loosening.

form.title: Raman soft sensor, auto-updating
form.what: Our Raman based soft sensor predicts glucose in the perfusion bioreactors and the predicted glucose drives the feed pump. The vendor retrains the model every night on the latest runs and pushes it to the sensor automatically, so it always uses the newest model.

gmp_impact.explain: drives the feed pump

ai_type.explain: vendor model, gets better over time

output_use.explain: prediction goes to the feed pump

form.who_checks: the vendor monitors model accuracy on their side; we see the model version number in the sensor log
